items.title: Sonnet 5.5 nearly matches Opus 5.5, now free-tier default
items.summary: Sonnet 5.5 jumps to 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus Sonnet 5's 10.3%, hits 80.1% on OSWorld computer-use tasks, and nearly matches Opus 5.5 on CursorBench (55.5% vs 57.8%) and GDPval-AA (1,844 vs 1,846). Pricing stays at $2/$10 per million tokens, and it now powers claude.ai's free tier. (2 minute read)

items.title: Adding "do not guess" cut hallucinated claims from 71% to 20%
items.summary: A single added instruction, "do not guess," dropped a benchmark's rate of fabricated claims from 71% to 20% with no other prompt changes. (1 minute read)

items.title: Kaggle's Game Arena pits LLMs against each other in chess, poker
items.summary: Kaggle's Game Arena evaluates LLMs by having them play head-to-head in Chess, Poker, and Werewolf, covering perfect-information, imperfect-information, and multiplayer settings. Because opponents keep improving, the benchmark resists the saturation that static leaderboards hit. A way to track strategic reasoning without waiting for the next benchmark to get memorized. (2 minute read)

items.title: Anthropic's IPO filing details its AI strategy and costs
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus lays out the company's AI strategy alongside its surging costs, per Reuters' review of the filing. (1 minute read)

items.title: World Labs is joining AMD
items.summary: World Labs, Fei-Fei Li's spatial-intelligence startup, announced it is joining AMD. (1 minute read)

items.title: Open TTS server hits 10 req/s, sub-50ms latency on one H100
items.summary: nari-qwen3-tts wraps the open Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice weights in a serving stack that handles 10 requests per second with sub-50ms p95 time-to-first-audio on a single H100. It ships three tunable profiles trading off latency against throughput, under Apache 2.0. Drop-in TTS serving without training or licensing a proprietary model. (2 minute read)

items.title: EAServe fixes GPU starvation in multimodal LLM serving
items.summary: Multimodal LLM serving splits into three stages, Encode, Prefill, and Decode, but existing systems treat Encode as a bolt-on service, leaving its GPUs underused while Prefill and Decode starve downstream. EAServe instead repositions Encode as a control point that regulates request flow into the rest of the pipeline. (2 minute read)

items.title: When local LLMs can replace frontier-model calls, quantified
items.summary: Touchstone routes network-automation tasks to small local models (1-8B params) only when a cheap deterministic check can verify the output, escalating the rest to a frontier LLM. On conflict-detection and intent-translation it hits 98.6% and 93.8% accuracy while escalating just 16-17% of requests. Keep sensitive configs local whenever a task admits a cheap correctness check. (2 minute read)
